fields.objective: Maintain and passage mammalian cell lines
fields.materials:
- Cell line of interest
- Complete growth medium
- PBS (phosphate-buffered saline)
- Trypsin-EDTA (0.25%) or cell dissociation solution
- Cell culture flasks/plates
- Hemocytometer or automated cell counter
- Trypan blue
- Centrifuge
- 37°C incubator with 5% CO2
- Biosafety cabinet
- 70% ethanol

protocol.description:
Preparation:
  - Pre-warm medium, PBS, and trypsin in 37°C water bath
  - Sterilize biosafety cabinet with 70% ethanol
  - Label new flasks with cell line, passage number, and date

Remove Old Medium:
  - Examine cells under microscope, note confluence and morphology
  - Aspirate medium from flask

Wash Cells:
  - Add PBS to wash cells (5-10 mL for T75 flask)
  - Gently rock flask
  - Aspirate PBS

Trypsinization:
  - Add trypsin-EDTA (2-3 mL for T75 flask)
  - Rock to cover all cells
  - Incubate at 37°C for 3-5 minutes
  - Tap flask to dislodge cells
  - Check under microscope to confirm detachment

Neutralize Trypsin:
  - Add complete medium (equal or greater volume than trypsin)
  - Mix by pipetting up and down gently
  - Transfer to sterile centrifuge tube

Centrifugation:
  - Centrifuge at 200-300 x g for 5 minutes
  - Aspirate supernatant carefully
  - Resuspend pellet in fresh medium

Cell Counting:
  - Mix cell suspension 1:1 with trypan blue
  - Load into hemocytometer
  - Count viable (clear) cells
  - Calculate cell concentration and viability

Seeding:
  - Dilute cells to desired seeding density
  - Add appropriate volume to new flask
  - Add complete medium to final volume
  - Gently rock to distribute cells evenly

Incubation:
  - Label flask with cell line, passage number, date, and initials
  - Return to 37°C incubator with 5% CO2
  - Monitor daily for growth and contamination

fields.observations:
- Record cell morphology
- Note any contamination or abnormalities
- Document growth rate
- Track passage number
